results.evidence: hazards[0], watch_out[0] and the wall waypoint note all say PG13; the Mountain Project area page lists Wright-Pond as 5.11a/b trad PG13. Only obj_haz says R. The route page calls P1 'a bold lead' but gives no R rating.

The Wright-Pond route page gives 600 ft (182 m), 4 pitches; the independently written Narcos page and its trip report give 600 ft for the neighbouring line that tops out at the same finish on the same wall. 244 m (800 ft) exceeds even the 200 m sum of the rope-length pitch figures, which run diagonally (P1 follows an arch left, P2 traverses a bolted face), so ~183 m of height is consistent with them.

The Mountain Project area pin gives 6,263 ft at 48.54975,-120.6435, but USGS 1 m ground at that same coordinate reads ~6,397 ft and nearby points range 6,240-6,433 ft, so the pin does not pin down either the base or the top. With ~600 ft of climbing (not 800), a 5,800 ft base would top out ~6,400 ft, so 6,263 may be a mid-face value; the 5,800 ft figure lives only in bivy[] (off-limits here). gain_ft 1312 has no outside source. No two sources state base or top elevations; no patch.

results.fact: Which Wright-Pond anchors Narcos shares for bail
results.correct_value: Narcos joins Wright-Pond in its P3 right-facing corner and shares the bolted belay at the top of Wright-Pond's third pitch, then finishes on Wright-Pond's last pitch
results.evidence: The Narcos page says P4 steps right into a right-facing corner, 'you are now on the Wright-Pond', and follows it to a bolted belay; P5 finishes as Wright-Pond's last pitch. The Wright-Pond page (separate author) describes its P3 as the right-facing corner ending at a bolted belay below the P4 corner/chimney, with P1 and P2 belays low on the left side of the wall. So the shared bolted station is Wright-Pond's P3 anchor, not its P1/P2 stations; overview and pitch_detail are consistent with this.

results.evidence: USGS ground at the trailhead pin reads ~4,470 ft and the wall pin area ~6,240-6,430 ft, so 2,700 ft looks high for car-to-car, but no outside source states a gain figure for this route and the rules forbid computing one from elevations. No patch.

Sources give only time (1-1.5 hr to the shoulder) and the first leg (1/4 mile on the old road bed to a double cairn); none gives a total approach distance. Straight-line trailhead to wall pin is ~0.7 mi, so 1.2 mi is plausible and 1.5-2 mi possibly high, but nothing external settles it. No patch.
